# iliad-062 — new renderings (10.390–481)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα Δόλων, ὑπὸ δ’ ἔτρεμε γυῖα (10.390, whole line) | "Him then answered Dolon, and beneath trembled his limbs:" | "Then Dolon answered him, and his limbs trembled beneath him:" | "shook", "his body shook" (γυῖα is "limbs", as in the table's γυῖα λάβῃ κάματος); built on the table's τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα formulas, ὑπό kept as "beneath" |
| θοὴν διὰ νύκτα μέλαιναν (10.394, 10.468) | "through the swift black night" | "through the swift black night" | "the dark night", "the swift night" (drops μέλαιναν), "the black night" (that is the shipped νύκτα μέλαιναν, 10.297, without θοήν); θοός keeps "swift" even of night |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε Δόλων Εὐμήδεος υἱός (10.412, whole line) | "Him then in turn addressed Dolon, Eumedes’ son:" | "Then Dolon, the son of Eumedes, spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); built on the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε formulas, with the name as at 10.314 (iliad-061) |
| τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα Δόλων Εὐμήδεος υἱός (10.426, whole line) | "Him then answered Dolon, Eumedes’ son:" | "Then Dolon, the son of Eumedes, answered him:" | "addressed … in turn" (reserved for αὖτε προσέειπε); the ἠμείβετ’ counterpart of 10.412 |
| ἀλεγεινοὶ … δαμήμεναι ἠδ’ ὀχέεσθαι (10.402–403, of the horses of Achilles) | "grievous … to be tamed and to be driven" | "grievous … to tame and to drive" (+ note: ὀχέομαι "be carried", said of a team) | "hard", "difficult" (the house word for ἀλεγεινός is "grievous"), "troublesome"; δαμάζω is "tame" of horses and "overcome" of men (10.397, 10.411), and the note says it is one verb |
| βουληφόροι (10.414) | "counsel-bearers" | "councillors" | "counsellors", "advisers", "leaders"; βουλή is "plan" / "counsel" and φέρω "bear" |
| βουλὰς βουλεύει (10.415) | "is taking counsels" | "is holding counsel" | "plotting plans", "devising"; the cognate figure is kept in `l`, and βουλεύω of an enemy's flight at 10.398 stays "plot" |
| φυλακαί (10.408, 10.416) | "watches" | "watches" | "guards" (reserved for φύλακες), "guard-posts", "sentries" (φυλακτῆρες); follows the table's φυλακή "the watch" |
| κεκριμένη (φυλακή, 10.417) | "picked-out" | "set apart" (+ note: κρίνω "separate, pick out") | "chosen", "regular", "proper" (each decides the sense) |
| ἐσχάραι (πυρὸς ἐσχάραι, 10.418) | "hearths of fire" | "hearth-fires" | "campfires", "watch-fires", "braziers"; ἐσχάρα is the hearth |
| ἐγρηγόρθασι (10.419) | "are awake" | "are awake" | "have woken", "are on the alert"; the perfect with the force of a present |
| πολύκλητοι ἐπίκουροι (10.420) | "the much-summoned allies" | "the allies, summoned from many places" | "famous allies" (that is κλειτοί, 3.451), "far-called", "many-called"; ἐπίκουρος keeps "ally" |
| εὐναί (10.408, 10.464, 10.473 ff.) | "beds" | "sleeping-places" | "lairs", "couches" (reserved for εὐνή 7.342), "camps"; the plural is the places men lie down, as at 2.783 |
| ἀγέρωχοι (Μυσοί τ’ ἀγέρωχοι, 10.430) | "lofty" | "lofty" (+ note: meaning not known) | "proud", "high-spirited", "haughty"; Odyssey table (11.286) and 2.654, unchanged |
| ἱππόμαχοι (Φρύγες ἱππόμαχοι, 10.431) | "horse-fighting" | "horse-fighting" (+ note: on horseback or from chariots is not said) | "charioteers", "cavalry", "who fight on horseback", "horsemen" (each decides the question); ἵππος + μάχομαι |
| ἀπάνευθε (10.425, 10.434) | "apart" | "apart" / "apart from them" | "far off", "alone"; ἀπάνευθε is "apart" in both places |
| νεήλυδες (10.434) | "newcomers" | "new arrivals" | "recruits", "strangers", "newly arrived" in `l`; νέος + ἔρχομαι |
| ἔσχατοι ἄλλων (10.434) | "last of the others" | "the last of the others" | "farthest", "outermost", "on the edge" (each decides that the position is spatial) |
| λευκότεροι χιόνος, θείειν δ’ ἀνέμοισιν ὁμοῖοι (10.437) | "whiter than snow, and in running like the winds" | "whiter than snow, and for running like the winds" | "swift as the wind", "fleet as the gale"; θείειν "to run" is kept as the point of likeness |
| ἅρμα … χρυσῷ τε καὶ ἀργύρῳ εὖ ἤσκηται (10.438) | "his chariot with gold and with silver is well wrought" | "his chariot is finely worked with gold and silver" | "adorned", "inlaid", "overlaid"; ἀσκέω "work with skill", kept apart from ποικίλος "intricate" (ποικίλα χαλκῷ, 10.393) |
| τεύχεα χρύσεια πελώρια θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι (10.439) | "armour of gold, huge, a wonder to behold" | "golden armour, huge, a wonder to look at" | "monstrous marvel" (θαῦμα πελώριον, 9.190, a different phrase: there the Cyclops' word), "gigantic", "marvellous"; πελώριος keeps "huge" (3.166, 5.594) |
| καταθνητοῖσιν ἄνδρεσσιν … ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν (10.440–441) | "those liable to death men … the immortal gods" | "men who are liable to death … the immortal gods" | "mortal men" (θνητοῖσι, 10.403, is "mortal"), "men who die"; follows the table's καταθνητός "liable to death" |
| νηλέϊ δεσμῷ (10.443) | "a pitiless bond" | "a pitiless bond" | "cruel fetters", "ruthless bonds", "merciless chains"; νηλεής "pitiless" (4.348), δεσμός "bond" |
| κατ’ αἶσαν ἔειπον (10.445) | "in due measure I spoke" | "I spoke in due measure" | "rightly", "fairly", "truly"; follows the table's κατ’ αἶσαν "in due measure" (3.59) |
| ἠὲ … ἦε καὶ οὐκί (10.445) | "or … or not" | "or not" | "or else not", "or perhaps not"; οὐκί is οὐ |
| μὴ δή μοι φύξίν γε … ἐμβάλλεο θυμῷ (10.447) | "Do not now, for me, flight … put into your heart" | "Do not, I tell you, … put thoughts of flight into your heart" | "do not even think of fleeing", "give up hope of escape"; μοι is an ethic dative, carried by "I tell you" in `i`; φύξις "flight" as in 10.398 |
| ἐσθλά περ ἀγγείλας (10.448) | "though good things you have reported" | "though what you have reported is good" | "although you brought good news", "bringing tidings", "though you spoke well"; ἀγγέλλω "report" |
| ἀπολύσομεν ἠὲ μεθῶμεν (10.449) | "release … or let go" | "release … or let go" | "set free", "send away"; ἀπολύω keeps "release" (the table's λύσαιτε "release") and μεθίημι "let go" |
| ἐναντίβιον πολεμίξων (10.451) | "head-on to fight" | "to fight us head-on" | "face to face", "in open battle"; follows the table's ἐναντίβιον "head-on" (8.255) |
| πῆμα … Ἀργείοισιν (10.453) | "a woe to the Argives" | "a woe to the Argives" | "bane", "plague", "scourge"; follows the table's πῆμα "woe" |
| ἦ, καὶ ὃ μέν … ὃ δ’ (10.454–455) | "He spoke, and the one … but the other" | "So he said, and Dolon … but Diomedes" | "He spoke, and Dolon", "the former … the latter"; the table's ἦ ῥα καί "He spoke, and" / "So he said, and", with the two pronouns named in `i` (the note says the Greek names neither) |
| γενείου … ἁψάμενος λίσσεσθαι (10.454–455) | "by the chin … having touched to beg" | "to touch him by the chin … and plead with him" | "take his chin", "seize his beard", "clasp his face"; ἅπτομαι "touch" with the genitive, and the note says the gesture is a suppliant’s |
| ἀΐξας … ἀπὸ δ’ ἄμφω κέρσε τένοντε (10.456) | "darting, and both tendons cut off" | "darted at him … and cut through both tendons" | "severed the sinews", "hacked through"; ἀΐσσω keeps "darting" (5.81, 8.87) |
| κτιδέην κυνέην · λυκέην (10.458–459) | "the weasel-skin helmet" · "the wolfskin" | "the weasel-skin helmet" · "the wolfskin" | "marten-skin cap" (the table's κτιδέη κυνέη, 10.335), "wolf-pelt cap"; λυκέη is the adjective alone, the hide of 10.334 |
| τόξα παλίντονα (10.459) | "the back-stretched bow" | "the back-stretched bow" | "the springy bow", "the recurved bow"; follows iliad-048's παλίντονα τόξα (8.266) |
| Ἀθηναίῃ ληΐτιδι (10.460) | "Athena, the spoil-giving" | "Athena, giver of spoil" (+ note: usual explanation, not certain) | "Athena of the booty", "plunder-bringing", "raider"; ληΐς "booty", and the note says giver rather than keeper is the usual view |
| ὑψόσ’ ἀνέσχεθε χειρὶ καὶ εὐχόμενος ἔπος ηὔδα (10.461) | "high held up in his hand, and praying spoke a word" | "held these up high in his hand … and said, praying" | "raised aloft", "lifted up"; εὔχομαι is "pray" here (to a goddess, not "declare"), ἔπος ηὔδα "spoke a word" as at 10.377 |
| χαῖρε θεὰ τοῖσδεσσι (10.462) | "Be glad, goddess, in these" | "Be glad of these, goddess" | "Welcome, goddess" (the greeting, the table's χαῖρε, ξεῖνε), "Hail", "Rejoice in these"; χαίρω + dative of the gift is "be glad of", not the greeting |
| σὲ γὰρ πρώτην … ἐπιδωσόμεθ’ (10.462–463) | "for you first … we shall give to" | "it is you we shall make our offerings to, first of all the immortals" (+ note: sense with the accusative not secure) | "call upon", "pay honour to", "give you gifts"; ἐπιδίδωμι "give in addition, give over", the note saying the context decides |
| πέμψον ἐπὶ Θρῃκῶν ἀνδρῶν ἵππους τε καὶ εὐνάς (10.464) | "send us to the Thracian men’s horses and beds" | "send us on again to the horses and the sleeping-places of the Thracian men" | "lead us to", "guide us to"; πέμπω "send", the object ‘us’ understood |
| ὣς ἄρ’ ἐφώνησεν, καὶ ἀπὸ ἕθεν ὑψόσ’ ἀείρας θῆκεν (10.465–466) | "So then he spoke, and from himself high raising he set them" | "So he spoke, and, raising the spoils high, away from himself, set them up" | "put them down", "laid them down"; follows the table's ὣς ἄρ’ ἐφώνησεν καὶ ἀπὸ ἕο τόξον ἔθηκε (21.163), with θῆκεν ἀνά "set up on" |
| δέελον σῆμα (10.466) | "a conspicuous sign" | "a conspicuous sign" (+ note: δέελος rare, sense from context) | "a clear mark", "a landmark", "a visible token", "tomb" (that is σῆμα of a grave, 2.814); σῆμα "sign" as in the table (20.111) |
| ἐριθηλέας ὄζους (10.467) | "the luxuriant boughs" | "the luxuriant boughs" | "leafy", "thick-leaved", "flourishing"; ἐρι- + θάλλω |
| μὴ λάθοι αὖτις ἰόντε (10.468) | "so that it should not escape them going again" | "so that it would not escape the two of them when they came back" | "lest they miss it", "that they might not lose it"; λανθάνω "escape the notice of", the subject being the marked place |
| τέλος (Θρῃκῶν ἀνδρῶν τέλος, 10.470) | "company" | "company" | "end" (the table's τέλος θανάτοιο), "troop", "host", "band"; τέλος here is a body of men |
| τριστοιχί (10.473) | "in three rows" | "in three rows" | "in three ranks", "in a triple line" |
| δίζυγες ἵπποι (10.473) | "a yoked pair of horses" | "a yoked pair of horses" | "twin horses", "a two-horse team", "paired"; δίζυξ "yoked in a pair" |
| ἐξ ἐπιδιφριάδος πυμάτης ἱμᾶσι δέδεντο (10.475) | "from the outermost chariot-rail with straps were tied" | "were tied with straps to the outermost chariot-rail" (+ note: which part of the chariot is not certain) | "the chariot-rim", "the chariot-board", "the last rail"; ἱμάς "strap" (8.544) |
| προπάροιθεν ἰδών (10.476) | "having seen ahead" | "saw him ahead" | "first", "before the rest", "seeing him in front"; προπάροιθεν "in front, ahead" |
| πίφαυσκε (10.478) | "made known" | "made known to us" | "pointed out", "told of", "revealed"; πιφαύσκω "make known" |
| κρατερὸν μένος (πρόφερε κρατερὸν μένος, 10.479) | "bring forward strong might" | "put forth your strong might" | "show your courage", "your fury", "rouse your strength"; follows the table's κρατερὸν μένος "strong might" (the Iliad row for Ἕκτορος … κρατερὸν μένος), with μένος "might" |
| μέλεον (ἑστάμεναι μέλεον, 10.480) | "idle" | "idle" | "in vain", "wretched", "useless"; the note says ‘to no purpose’ is the sense and ‘wretched’ the usual meaning of the adjective |
| μελήσουσιν δ’ ἐμοὶ ἵπποι (10.481) | "the horses will be a care to me" | "the horses will be my concern" | "I will see to", "I shall take care of the horses"; μέλω "be a care to" |

Departures from the Odyssey and from published Iliad English: none. The reused lines (10.397–399, 10.400, 10.405, 10.423, 10.446, 10.457) take the published English unchanged.
